admin.bufferHint: A buffer extends the map beyond the boundary, so a trail that crosses it is not cut off mid-route.
admin.filter: Filter {n} entries by name or canton
admin.title: Administrative units
app.title: swisstopo2garmin
area.exchangeHelp: GeoJSON, as QGIS and geojson.io read and write it. Importing replaces the current selection.
area.exportTitle: Where should the selection be saved?
area.method.drawHelp: Pick a tool below the map, then drag. Once drawn, the shape can be reshaped and moved.
area.searchHelp: Names are matched from the start and ignore case and accents, so “zurich” finds Zürich.
area.wholeHelp: About 41,300 km². Larger than any single device map, so it is built as several map sets.
budget.over: About {over} too large for this device's {budget} budget.
build.splitCannotFit: Even split this far, each part is still estimated over the device's budget. Reduce the area, coarsen the contours, or switch off layers you do not need.
build.splitHint: Each file is a separate map on the device, with its own name. Build them one at a time; if one fails the others are unaffected.
build.splitTitle: This area needs {n} separate map files
build.unrecognised: This failure is not one the app recognises, so there is no specific advice. The details below are what a bug report needs.
content.addressesHint: Search a street and house number on the device. Needs the address register on the Data screen — swissTLM3D has street names but no house numbers. Adds a searchable point per building.
content.contourHint: Contours dominate output size. 20 m suits most uses; 10 m doubles their contribution.
content.intro: Presets add a themed network on top of the base topographic map.
content.labelsHint: Local uses whatever each place is called where it is, which is how Swiss maps are normally drawn. The other options need swissNAMES3D, and a place with no name in that language keeps its local one.
content.needsData: Needs {what} — download it on the Data screen.
content.paletteHint: The winter scheme uses swisstopo's own Winter national map colours: the base map steps back so ski and snowshoe routes read on top of it.
content.reliefHint: Relief is rendered by the device. Detailed can look very dark in the Alps.
content.reliefUnsupported: This device profile does not report relief support.
content.routingHint: Lets the device navigate along the roads and paths, not only draw them. Adds roughly 34 bytes per road feature — about 12 % on a typical map.
content.routingWarning: Not yet verified on a device. Check any route it gives you against the road signs before following it, and report anything wrong.
content.slopeHint: Computed from the elevation data, in swisstopo's own classes: 30–35°, 35–40°, 40–45°, 45–50° and over 50°. Drawn as a hatch so the map underneath stays readable. Adds roughly 3.5 MB per 1,000 km² in alpine terrain, and much less where the ground is gentle.
data.checking: Checking swisstopo for the latest release…
data.chooseTitle: Where should map data be stored?
data.clearHint: Both can be deleted safely: elevation tiles are downloaded again when needed, and build files are rebuilt. Downloaded datasets and saved recipes are untouched.
data.envOverride: S2G_CACHE is set in the environment and overrides this setting.
data.inflateNote: The archive is inflated while downloading, so only the final file uses disk space.
data.intro: Maps are built from swisstopo open data. The national swissTLM3D dataset is downloaded once per release.
data.noMove: Nothing is copied. Datasets already downloaded stay in {path} and will be downloaded again in the new folder.
data.progress.label: Download progress
data.spaceHint: swissTLM3D alone needs about 10 GB, plus elevation tiles and build working files. Allow 20 GB.
data.staleRelease: Offline — release information last checked {when}, so a newer release may exist.
data.title: Source data
device.intro: Pick the device the map is for. It sets the size budget and the cartography detail.
device.limits.intro: Garmin publishes none of these limits, so most are community reports carrying a safety margin. If you have measured your own device, say so here: your number replaces both the estimate and its margin, and survives app updates.
device.limits.notePlaceholder: e.g. filled it until the device refused to load the map
device.limits.title: Limits measured yourself
device.mtpHint: The device is in MTP mode, which macOS cannot mount as a drive. Many Garmin devices can switch: on the device, look for Settings → System → USB Mode → Garmin, then reconnect. Recent Edge models have no such setting — for those, copy the file instead.
device.unverifiedHint: These limits are not measured, so a safety margin is applied.
device.usbOnly: Connected, but not available as a drive
estimate.areaOnly: Estimated from area alone — swissTLM3D is not downloaded, so feature counts are unknown.
estimate.calibrated: Accuracy improves as you build: this estimate is tuned to your last {n} maps.
estimate.shippedModel: From the shipped model, fitted on test builds. It will adapt to your own areas as you build.
install.backup: Keep a backup of the existing file
install.eject: Eject the device safely before unplugging it.
install.exportHint: Use this when the device is in MTP mode, when the card is in a reader, or whenever you would rather copy the file yourself. Put it in the folder below, under exactly that name.
install.exportTitle: Where should the map be saved?
install.noDeviceHint: Connect the device by USB and let it mount, then scan again. You can also copy the file manually.
install.tooBig: Not enough free space on the device.
install.willReplace: A map file already exists at this path and will be replaced.
layers.intro: Every layer is included unless you switch it off here. Fewer layers means a smaller file.
layers.title: Layers
layers.trailsNote: Swiss hiking trails are an attribute of the road layer, so they cannot be switched off on their own — turning roads off removes the trails with them.
map.editDragging: Drag to reshape. Release to apply.
map.editHint: Drag a corner to reshape, the middle to move it, or a small point to add a corner.
map.editHintCircle: Drag the blue centre to move it, the ring handle to change the radius.
map.polygonHint: Click each corner, double-click to finish
preset.full.desc: Everything, with 10 m contours. Largest file.
preset.hiking.desc: Swiss trail classes, lifts and cableways.
preset.skimo.desc: SAC ski routes, snowshoe and winter hiking trails.
recipes.name: Recipe name
recipes.title: Saved recipes
recovery.resumeHint: The extracted data and contours survived, so resuming skips most of the work.
recovery.strays: {count} map-compiler process(es) from those builds are still running and are using a processor core.
recovery.title: {count} build(s) did not finish last time
remedy.coarserContours: Use a wider contour interval — contours are the largest part of a map.
remedy.fewerLayers: Turn off layers you do not need in the layer panel.
remedy.splitIntoMapSets: Build several map sets and switch between them on the device — this keeps the whole area.
source.skitouren: SAC ski routes — tours and network
step.locked.build: Choose a device and an area first.
track.hint: GPX tracks and routes, or Garmin FIT courses. The map area becomes a corridor around the route.
track.name: Route
track.partlyOutside: Part of this route lies outside the swisstopo coverage area; only the Swiss part will be mapped.
content.rasterHint: Adds the swisstopo paper map itself as a picture laid over the map, so the device shows the rock drawing and the typography you know from the printed sheet. A separate file in Garmin/CustomMaps, not part of the map.
content.rasterPlan: {tiles} tiles ({cols} × {rows}) at {res} m per pixel, about {size} and {seconds} s to download.
content.rasterWarning: Not yet verified on a device. The overlay is limited to 100 tiles across all custom maps on the device, which covers about 12 × 12 km at full sharpness.
build.raster: Paper-map overlay: {tiles} tiles at {res} m per pixel, {size}.
install.rasterUnavailable: This device has no known custom-map limits, so the overlay will not be installed. The map itself will be.
install.rasterFailed: The map was installed but the paper-map overlay was not: {message}
device.mtpOnly: This model has no USB-mode setting: MTP is the only mode it offers, so there is nothing to change on the device. macOS cannot mount MTP as a drive.
device.mtpCopy: Build the map, then copy the file into the Garmin folder on the device. On macOS use a tool such as OpenMTP; on Windows, File Explorer speaks MTP natively. The build step shows where the file is, and Export to folder puts a copy wherever you like.
